alignment.note: Greek καί and Latin Et open the verse with paratactic conjunction; the Peshitta omits the connective entirely, beginning directly with the verb ܐܡܪ ('he said'), a stylistic feature of Syriac narrative that does not require an introductory copula.

Greek ἔλεγεν and Latin dicebat are imperfect ('he was saying', continuous aspect), whereas the Syriac ܐܡܪ is a perfect/simple past ('he said'); Syriac lacks a morphological imperfect of this nuance and renders the durative Greek with its unmarked past form.
αὐτοῖς / ܠܗܘܢ / eis; the Vulgate colon (index 3) marks the onset of direct speech.

Greek οὔπω and Latin nondum render 'not yet' as a single adverb, while the Peshitta employs the analytic phrase ܠܐ ܥܕܡܐ ܠܗܫܐ ('not until now'), a periphrastic expansion idiomatic to Syriac that conveys the identical temporal sense.

The interrogative (πῶς / Quomodo / ܐܝܟܘ, 'how') stands after the negative adverb in Greek and Latin but is fronted to the head of the clause in the Peshitta, reflecting Syriac preference for placing the interrogative element early.

Greek συνίετε and Latin intelligitis encode the second-person plural subject within the verb, whereas the Peshitta uses the participle ܡܣܬܟܠܝܢ with the explicit enclitic pronoun ܐܢܬܘܢ ('you'), the standard Syriac participial construction for the present tense that supplies the pronoun as a separate token.
Interrogative punctuation; the Greek question mark is fused to συνίετε;¶ in token 5, so only the Vulgate question mark stands as an independent token.
